meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here? My son got a zero, and nobody called me.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What was the zero for?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend, Hale. He drafted somewhere else and pasted it in here. That's not a crime.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
I'll ask him tonight. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ, and kids misquote. Which edition is that, Hale?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll search it myself tonight. Did you speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. We'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Tonight, in writing, with the mark replacing the zero and nothing on his file.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll ask him tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in the email, and I'll answer in writing.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still require written confirmation of those terms, including that nothing goes on his file, and I will confirm with Owen whether the date works. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing from you tonight and Owen's availability confirmed; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and, when she said he drafted elsewhere, invited the dated draft she could check, which moved her to protecting his record.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground, since you never accused Owen and never leaned on a software score.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the writing late on an October night, which came close to that, though it proves nothing about the essay and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: She asked whether you spoke to Owen before the zero went in and you moved on to the next document, so answer that directly, since it is the first step of the school's own procedure.
